metadata.name: jobs
metadata.displayName: jobs - Display status of shell jobs
metadata.description: List active and stopped jobs in the current shell

installation.note: jobs is a shell built-in (commonly in bash), not a standalone binary

overview.summary: The jobs command lists the jobs associated with the current shell session. Each job has a job number (e.g., [1], [2]) used with fg and bg. Jobs can be running, stopped, or in the background.
when_to_use: See which jobs are running or stopped in the current terminal
Get job numbers to use with fg or bg
Check status before bringing a job to the foreground

syntax.description: Without arguments, jobs lists all jobs. You can optionally filter by job number or use options to show process IDs.

options.description: Show process IDs in addition to job information
options.use_case: When you need PIDs for kill or other process tools

options.description: Show only process IDs of job processes
options.use_case: For scripting when you need just PIDs

examples.title: List all jobs
examples.description: Show running and stopped jobs with their job numbers
examples.use_case: See what is running in the background or suspended

examples.title: List jobs with PIDs
examples.description: Show job numbers and process IDs
examples.use_case: When you need to kill or inspect a specific process

related_commands.description: Resume a stopped job in the background
Bring a job to the foreground
Send signals to processes; use job numbers with % (e.g., kill %1)
